rows.title: Basic Police Academy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and apply criminal law as it applies to the duties of a police officer.
Interpret legally required principles and procedures associated with the duties of a police officer.
Implement appropriate patrol and investigation procedures.
Write proper law enforcement reports.
Employ legally approved defensive policing tactics and appropriate levels of use of force.

rows.title: Legal Aspects of Evidence
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the reasons and purposes for the Rules of Evidence.
Differentiate the various forms of admissible evidence and the role that evidence plays in the judicial process.
Explain the application of the Fourth Amendment in protecting people from unreasonable searches and seizures by the government.
Describe how the Miranda decision applies to a defendant's legal rights and waiver of rights.

rows.title: Organized Crime
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply psychological and sociological theories to explain youth involvement in organized crime.
Compare the social and cultural influences of organized crime among various ethnicities.
Analyze the practices and procedures used to combat organized crime.
Explain the cultural competencies in investigating organized crime using methods of inquiry used by the social and behavioral sciences.

rows.title: Criminal Justice, Drugs, Crime, and the Law
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the historical and ongoing interface among drug use, the drug trade, and crime.
Differentiate patterns of licit and illicit drug use and types of treatment programs
Articulate the origins and continued influence of the "war on drugs"
Examine drug laws and criminal justice policies intended to reduce offender drug use.

rows.title: Crime Scene Documentation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Utilize appropriate methods to document, collect, and preserve commonly encountered evidence in a variety of crime scene exercises.
Implement knowledge of camera functions and concepts to solve various photographic problems that occur in crime scene photography.
Reconstruct crime scenes using the scientific method and evidence-based logic.
Analyze types and sources of potential error at the crime scene.

rows.title: Community Corrections
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the roles and functions of probation and parole officers.
Analyze the symbiotic and intersectional relationships between parole, probation, policing, courts and institutional corrections and the community.
Evaluate the historical and social context in which community corrections developed in response to criminal behavior.
Evaluate the effectiveness of community-based correction programs to various models of incarceration and containment.

rows.title: African American Consciousness
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the intersection of race and racism in the arenas of African American culture and consciousness.
Interpret definitions and theories of culture and culture change that are found in African American scholarly literature.

Identify how the struggle, resistance, solidarity of African Americans resulted in distinct expressions of culture and consciousness, as well as how multiculturalism has created patterns of convergence with Anglo-American culture and consciousness.

Describe the ways in which African American oral lore and popular music forms have been expressions of anti-racism and social justice instrumental in the movement for a more just and equitable society.
Evaluate the major expressions of the African American intellectual tradition as manifested in the writings of the African American intelligentsia.

rows.title: African American Women in the U.S.
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Classify traditional theories, institutional structures, and practices, including colonialism, that have restricted freedoms and perpetuated oppression of African and African American women in the U.S.

Analyze how the British and U.S. legal systems have both hindered and supported African and African American women in the U.S., allowing them to make important contributions while at the same time limiting their agency.
Interpret the resistance and political actions of individual women and social organizations in African American communities that have promoted racial and social justice, solidarity, and liberation.
Evaluate literary and artistic creations and contributions of African American women that have served as anti-racist and anti-colonial responses to U.S. history, culture, and society.
Articulate the relevance of social and historical theories applied to African American women in practical efforts to realize an equitable and just society.

rows.title: Latin American Cultures and Societies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish the non-western roles and values in the contemporary indigenous cultures of Latin America.
Analyze and contextualize the unique historical perspectives of the contemporary peoples of Latin America.
Critique the influences of non-Iberian cultures on Latin America.
Evaluate the role of the Indigenous people in the cultural history of Latin America.

rows.title: Archaeology and Prehistory
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Summarize the goals of archaeology and its subfields and specializations, including cultural resource management.
Analyze the changing features and theoretical perspectives of archaeology over time from earliest practitioners, through the Renaissance, the 19th and 20th centuries, and into the present.
Assess the nature and types of evidence found and studied in archaeology and contemporary scientific methods of studying that evidence.
Compare the major industries of prehistory as well as the origins of agriculture and civilization from the Lower Paleolithic through the Neolithic periods.
Synthesize the major trends and problems in New World archaeology.

rows.title: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology: Focus on U.S. Cultures
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discuss both historical and contemporary topics in U.S. culture from an anthropological perspective.
Apply anthropological methods of inquiry, including ethical research design, to understand contemporary phenomena in the United States, such as inequity.
Examine the major theoretical perspectives of anthropology used in the research of different communities in the United States.
Analyze the major cultural practices that create the ideology of a unified “U.S. Culture” and how this culture is recreated and contested

rows.title: Introduction to Architecture and Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish the various related professional careers in architecture, design and related fields.
Describe the education and experience necessary for a career development and professional licensing.
Analyze characteristics of building design, interior design, and urban design from images.
Articulate the significance of sustainability and diverse values of different design process in architecture, interior design, and related fields.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Building Construction
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate the impact of building codes on the selection of building systems
Assess the processes and techniques of building construction
Analyze materials and building systems in terms of their effect on sustainability and energy conservation
Assess how the processes by which buildings are designed and built influence the selection of building materials and systems

rows.title: AutoCAD I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create architectural drawings employing the standards and conventions of architectural graphic representations using AutoCAD.
Analyze an AutoCAD layering system and apply it to differentiate various drawing or model elements.
Synthesize separate AutoCAD drawings and models using external references in the coordination and collaboration of drawings.
Explain best practices in using AutoCAD for collaborative projects.

rows.title: Freehand Drawing I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create freehand sketches with shapes and forms using correct proportions without the use of straight edge tools.
Express form, value, and texture in freehand drawing with shades and shadows.
Analyze various line and tonal techniques used in freehand drawing for visual communication of the built enviornment.
Create freehand linear perspective drawings.

rows.title: Asian Art History
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the formal visual elements and techniques of works of Asian art in different media.
Compare the stylistic aspects and trends of Asian art.
Evaluate works of Asian art in relation to their cultural and historical context.
Differentiate the various Asian visual traditions.

rows.title: Women Through Art History
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the formal visual elements of individual works of art by women in different media.
Evaluate how artworks created by women fit or transgress specific art historical movements.
Analyze the historical, social, and gender factors that affected the methods and themes used by women artists.
Evaluate the reinterpretation of women artists through updated historical and feminist scholarship.
Explain the gender relevance of artworks by employing basic art historical methods and terminology.

rows.title: American Art
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and analyze the formal visual elements and techniques of individual works of American art in different media.
Compare the stylistic aspects and trends of American art.
Evaluate works of American art in relation to their cultural and historical context.
Define and distinguish the American visual tradition.

rows.title: Basic Design: 2-D Foundations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply design elements and principles of visual organization to create unified two-dimensional compositions that communicate a specific idea, feeling, and/or intent.
Evaluate a range of creative methods and platforms to examine how people communicate through art within the larger system of global art culture.
Analyze visual dynamics in artwork from diverse eras and cultures to illustrate the interdependence of content, form, and context.
Infer and apply ideas and methods from contemporary and historic art as a catalyst for creative expression.
Analyze the dynamic interrelationship between a whole and its parts that lead to the construction of well-designed and sound structures.

rows.title: Intermediate Drawing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intermediate-level drawing techniques effectively using a variety of dry and wet media.
Utilize drawing concepts and basic color theory to effectively and creatively solve problems at the intermediate level.
Analyze historical and contemporary drawings from diverse cultures to create expressive personal content.
Evaluate one’s own intermediate-level drawings and the work of peers in terms of formal qualities, technical skills and expressive content.

rows.title: Character Illustration
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create an expressive visual narrative theme and set a character in a particular time and space.
Experiment with range of drawing approaches and mixed media techniques to tell a visual story.
Develop an effective character utilizing portraiture and exaggeration techniques in order to establish personality.
Analyze and discuss artwork with regard to content and individual expression toward a work's potential revision.
Integrate art-historical research and technical skills into design and drawing of a costume on a human figure.

rows.title: Beginning Chinese Brush Painting
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply beginning-level Chinese brush painting and calligraphy techniques using traditional materials.
Utilize foundational brushstroke techniques, including the 26 basic strokes of Chinese calligraphy, to express cultural and artistic ideas.
Analyze the classic elements of Chinese painting and calligraphy in relation to their historical and cultural significance.
Evaluate one’s own beginning-level Chinese brush paintings and calligraphy, as well as the work of peers, in terms of composition, brush technique, and expressive qualities.
Demonstrate an understanding of balance, composition, and traditional Chinese stylistic approaches to representational flower painting at a beginning

rows.title: Beginning Ceramics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply control over materials and techniques to form and decorate ceramic artwork at a beginning level.
Apply the basics of three-dimensional design in the creation of ceramic artwork, integrating and utilizing terminology specific to the processes of the ceramic medium.
Employ critical thinking when developing ceramic forms and meeting aesthetic expectations.
Research historical examples so that the contemporary creation of ceramic artwork contributes to cultural development.

rows.title: Beginning Jewelry/Metal Arts
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and apply basic jewelry and metals techniques to develop pieces that relate to historical, conceptual, cultural, or contemporary issues, or address personal narrative.
Apply design principles and metals/jewelry terminology in analyzing and discussing jewelry or metalwork with regard to content and individual expression.
Explain and employ additive, reductive and manipulation working processes using traditional and non-traditional materials to reflect idea development in basic metalsmithing and jewelry.
Evaluate and problem solve during the design and creation of a work of art in three-dimensions.
Establish and practice safe working methods and employ good craftsmanship in the creation of jewelry and metal arts.

rows.title: Asian American Popular Culture
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess the role of popular culture and countercultures in defining Asian American identity.
Analyze the creation and evolution of popular culture through the lens of anti-colonialism, anti-racism, and equity for Asian Americans.
Analyze the intersections of culture, race, and identity in Asian American creative expression.
Apply theory and knowledge produced by Asian American communities in order to describe pop culture connections to their histories, contributions, oppression, and agency.
Evaluate pop culture representations of Asian Americans engaged in racial and social justice and their relevance to current and structural issues.

rows.title: Asian American Race Relations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define race relations using critical race theory and social analysis of realities and struggles that Asian American communities in the U.S. have faced.

Critique how struggle, resistance, racial and social justice experienced and enacted by Asian Americans are relevant to current group interactions and race relations in the U.S. between Asian Americans and other ethnic groups.
Analyze Asian American Studies frameworks affecting race relations, social science theory and knowledge produced by Asian Americans.
Engage critically with anti-racist issues and frame positions about racial incidents involving Asian Americans and the quest for an equitable society.

rows.title: Intro to Asian American Studies: Southeast Asian American Experiences
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and articulate concepts of race, ethnicity, and identity through the lens of colonialism, anti-racism, and equity for Southeast Asian Americans.

Apply Asian American Studies theories and knowledge to the histories, cultures, contributions, struggles, and agency of Southeast Asian American communities to analyze historic and contemporary issues, lived-experiences, critical events and social struggles and to distinguish this analysis from Orientalist representations.

Analyze critical intersections of race and racism in relation to class, gender, sexuality, religion, national origin, immigration status, language and/or age in Southeast Asian American communities through survey of Asian American Studies analysis of key events and examples.

Review critically through readings, writing, class lectures and discussions, how struggle, resistance, racial and social justice, solidarity, and liberation as experienced and enacted by Southeast Asian American groups are relevant to current and structural issues.

Describe and engage with anti-racist and anti-colonial issues and the practices and movements in Southeast Asian American communities building a just and equitable society, including active community participation, shared with the class.
Use an Ethnic Studies framework to describe the full diversity of the Southeast Asian American community in the United States.

rows.title: Filipino American Community
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the textured histories of Filipinx American communities from multiple perspectives, including an Ethnic Studies framework.

Analyze the history of United States government policies and their critical impact on Filipinx American communities by employing Asian American Studies concepts of race and racism, racialization, ethnicity, equity, ethno-centrism, Eurocentrism, white supremacy, self-determination, liberation, decolonization, sovereignty, imperialism, and anti-racism.

Describe and articulate the intersectional identities within Filipinx American communities in the United States, the intersection of race and racism as they relate to class, gender, national origin, immigration status, language, age, sexuality, religion.

Apply Ethnic Studies theories and methodologies, social and behavioral science, and Filipinx community knowledge to analyze critical events, histories, cultures, intellectual traditions, contributions, lived-experiences and social struggles in the Filipinx American experience, emphasizing agency and group-affirmation.

Engage actively with and explain anti-racist and anti-colonial issues shaping Filipinx American communities, including workplace justice, fair housing, equity for veterans, and the practices and movements to build a just and equitable society.

rows.title: Cosmic Evolution
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze theories and evidence about the structure, origin, evolution, and possible final states of the universe.
Interpret and assess models of the properties, formation, evolution, and interactions of large-scale structure, galaxies, stars, and planetary systems.
Differentiate the universe and its major components.
Distinguish the roles of fundamental particles, forces, and astrophysical processes in the universe.
Explain the relationship of human beings to astronomical objects and evolutionary history in terms of cosmic size and time scales.

rows.title: Galaxies and the Universe
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate the properties of the universe, large-scale structure, and galaxies, and of fundamental particles and forces.
Discuss the history of cosmology from the ancient to modern world.
Interpret the structure, origin, evolution of the universe and its large-scale structure from the perspective of physical cosmology.
Compare the types of galaxies, and their structure, formation, evolution, and interactions.
Describe major astrophysical phenomena at the galaxy and universe scales that remain unresolved.

rows.title: Bolted Panel Replacement
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and observe all auto body shop safety practices related to bolted panel repair and replacement.
Evaluate repair costs with detailed attention to estimation of bolted panel damage, materials, and labor time.
Describe vehicle structure types and materials and tools used in bolted panel repair and replacement.
Apply the basic steps of repairing or removing and replacing bolted panels on vehicles.

rows.title: Auto Body Welding
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and employ auto shop safety practices related to metal welding, heating, cutting, and joining various metals and plastics.
Evaluate repair costs with detailed attention to estimation of welding and installation of welded panels, parts and materials, and labor times.
Distinguish between various welding, heating, and cutting techniques and describe the use of appropriate equipment for those techniques.
Describe and apply methods used to remove and replace automotive structural parts and to restore corrosion protection.

rows.title: Intro to Automotive Mechanics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply appropriate safety procedures while handling automotive technology equipment
Select and employ appropriate tools and equipment to perform automotive diagnosis and basic repairs
Use technical service publications to diagnosis and repair basic automotive systems
Perform maintenance and light repair of major vehicle systems
Evaluate overall vehicle condition

rows.title: Engine Repair
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess automotive engine parts, operation, and nomenclature.
Diagnose and repair automotive engines.
Evaluate and adjust automotive engine component tolerances.

rows.title: Automotive Suspension and Steering
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess vehicle suspension system parts, operation, and nomenclature.
Diagnose and repair vehicle suspension components.
Evaluate and adjust vehicle wheel alignment settings.

rows.title: Introduction to Electronic Media
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze operational and regulatory issues related to broadcast electronic media.
Explain the history of electronic media technology and its impact on contemporary media systems.
Analyze and evaluate current trends in electronic media.
Evaluate issues regarding operations and business practices in contemporary electronic media.
Analyze the effects of media on individuals and society.

rows.title: Announcing and Performance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze written copy in order to prepare for vocal performance.
Demonstrate vocal and physical performance techniques for a range of performance styles appropriate for specific media formats.
Demonstrate proper classification and practical use of basic technology used in the audio and television performance environments.
Express appropriate techniques for developing and maintaining vocal health and performance skill.

rows.title: Pro Tools Mixing with Plugins
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use Pro Tools software to balance, sweeten, and automate a final mix of a music project.
Mix a multitrack music session using intermediate-level techniques with plugins to enhance the program material.
Remix and master a Pro Tools music session that includes Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) using intermediate-level bussing techniques.

rows.title: Interconnected Audio Systems
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the integration of and interconnection of audio equipment and applications.
Set up, operate, and maintain digital consoles connected to digital interface devices.
Route high resolution, multi-channel audio by connecting digital consoles, computers and digital signal processors.

rows.title: Studio Video Production
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and evaluate the aesthetics of video production processes.
Describe and operate the video, audio, and lighting equipment used in a studio television environment.
Describe and perform the responsibilities and roles of each technical and non-technical video production member in the television studio environment.
Work in a team to create and evaluate a studio video project with related preproduction steps and materials.

rows.title: Video Motion Graphics - Introduction
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess methods and use tools for creating motion graphics and effects within a digital 2D and 2.5D environment.
Compose motion graphic storytelling projects complying with specified quality, formats, and pre-production file requirements.
Develop projects from ideation to delivery and apply diverse motion graphics styles.
Apply knowledge of workforce protocol in the post-production environment.

rows.title: Digital Media Portfolio
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze online portfolios and portfolio platforms.
Create an effective digital portfolio and professional resume.
Evaluate creative work for inclusion in portfolio.

rows.title: Animal Biology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the chemical and cellular basis of animal life
Evaluate the ecological factors that determine the distribution of animal populations
Compare anatomy and physiology between groups of animals as they relate to survival
Assess the principles of animal classification and evolution
Compare the natural history and behavior of major animal groups

rows.title: General Human Anatomy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Develop a vocabulary of appropriate terminology to effectively communicate information related to anatomy.
Describe and analyze the interrelationship between structure and function in the human body.
Identify and describe the basic cellular and tissue structures specifically associated with each major system of the human body.
Identify and describe the basic gross anatomical structures of the organs associated with each major system of the human body.

rows.title: Exploring Neuroscience: An introduction to the Brain
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the functional anatomy/physiology of neurons and the organization of the human nervous system including sensory systems and coordination of output by motor systems.
Explain mechanisms associated with cellular events and their impact on larger scale neuronal processing.
Evaluate and relate multiple theories of synaptic plasticity to principles of Hebbian synapse formation, long-term potentiation and memory encoding.
Analyze topics associated with higher order cortical processing.
Distinguish similarities and differences between the processing of different sensory modalities
Appraise and synthesize new developments in the field of neuroscience.

rows.title: Introduction to Microbiology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct an argument for evolutionary theory using evidence provided by microbial life and describe how microbial biodiversity is generated, perpetuated, and adapts to distinct environments.
Apply principles of biochemistry and genetics to the growth, cooperation, and adaptations of microorganisms.
Analyze the interplay between a wide variety of microorganisms and the human immune system.
Predict how microorganisms will interact with other organisms and the environment using the principles of microbial ecology.
Investigate a variety of common microorganisms employing proper microbiological practices in a laboratory setting.
Analyze quantitative and qualitative scientific data generated in the microbiology laboratory.

rows.title: Introduction to Nutrition for Health Sciences
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use reliable scientific evidence to critique nutrition-relevant theories and dietary guidelines.
Diagram key steps in the digestion, absorption, and metabolism of nutrients for body processes.
Use reliable scientific evidence to predict the effects of nutrient imbalances on human health and disease outcomes.
Evaluate dietary recommendations at all stages of the human life cycle.
Explain how nutrition science impacts health policy.

rows.title: Introduction to Ecology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Organize basic scientific and ecological concepts on a variety of scales and levels.
Evaluate the validity of scientific information, particularly to make informed political and personal choices pertaining to ecology.
Analyze biotic and abiotic factors shaping ecosystems, community structure, population dynamics, and species' adaptations, particularly on the local level.
Apply models to explain the behavior of commonly occurring ecological phenomena.
Apply ecological theory and concepts in practical applications.

rows.title: Ecology of Point Reyes National Seashore
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify key drivers and processes that affect community structure and dynamics of Point Reyes National Seashore ecosystems
Apply ecological concepts to management of the biological communities of Point Reyes National Seashore.
Evaluate scientific information and apply it in the field to specific ecological observations.
Observe and identify the diversity of habitats within the Point Reyes National Seashore and their associated biota.

rows.title: Coastal Ecosystem Field Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify key drivers and processes that affect community structure and dynamics of coastal ecosystems.
Evaluate scientific information and apply it to field investigations.
Observe and identify key habitats and their associated flora and fauna in coastal ecosystems.
Apply ecological concepts to the management of biological communities in coastal ecosystems.

rows.title: Plants and Animals of California
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the major factors shaping the evolution of the plants and animals of California’s major ecoregions.
Analyze biotic and abiotic factors shaping species’ adaptations for the plants and animals of California’s major ecoregions.
Explain how biologists apply various experimental methods to generate data and form conclusions.
Evaluate how modem human society is impacting California's biodiversity and ecosystem functions and appraise alternatives to reduce these impacts.

rows.title: Business Law I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the current function and subject matter jurisdiction of courts in the U.S. legal system.
Identify and categorize legal problems commonly encountered by businesses, and explain recommended solutions.
Apply legal ethics to business practices.
Analyze contract problems to identify relevant legal issues and apply contract rules to predict likely outcomes.

rows.title: GLP and GMP Principles
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the historical events that led to the creation of good laboratory practices (GLP), good manufacturing practices (GMP) regulations, and the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).
Describe how the FDA ensures the safety and efficacy of drugs and biologics.
Describe the role of quality assurance (QA) and quality control (QC) in the development of drugs and biologics.
Apply principles of GLP and GMP to work in a regulated biotechnology setting.

rows.title: Mammalian Cell Culture
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply knowledge of cell biology concepts to prepare and maintain cells in culture.
Evaluate cell counts to calculate and prepare proper cell concentrations.
Apply proper and safe operation of cell culture lab equipment.
Describe theory of fluorescence and apply to cellular assays.
Record, analyze and discuss experimental data in industry standard laboratory formats.

rows.title: Enzyme Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA)
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the key principles of ELISA using industry-standard terminology.
Implement and carry out standard ELISA procedures.
Organize and analyze ELISA data in industry-standard format.
Describe applications of the ELISA technique in basic science, environmental, pharmaceutical, clinical, and industry laboratories.
Describe the standard methods used to develop polyclonal and monoclonal antibodies and their application in ELISA.

rows.title: Introduction to Biotechnology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Investigate scientific principles and biotechnology concepts by performing basic laboratory techniques.
Evaluate, document, and communicate data obtained from biotechnology investigations.
Apply concepts and principles in biotechnology to explain and analyze observations from scientific inquiry and investigation
Apply scientific concepts and principles to describe different fields of biotechnology industry, applications and impacts on society.
Identify careers and educational pathways in biotechnology.

rows.title: Introduction to Computer Aided Drafting - CAD I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Formulate a procedure to synthesize and build, in the most efficient manner possible, a completely dimensioned multi-view drawing of a machine part or building/structure, utilizing the drawing commands of CAD software.

Formulate a procedure to synthesize and build, in the most efficient manner possible, an isometric pictorial drawing of a machine part or building/structure, utilizing the drawing commands of CAD software.
Solve basic descriptive geometry problems using geometric constructions with CAD software.
Customize CAD software environmental variables and specific document settings to print or plot a technical drawing on various paper layouts.

rows.title: Part Modeling in SOLIDWORKS®
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:

rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and perform beginning modern dance technique, vocabulary, and combinations.
Explain and demonstrate correct body alignment both static and dynamic as it applies to beginning modern dance.
Identify and perform the elements of a beginning modern dance class to build strength, flexibility, endurance, and coordination.
Perform basic dance movements in conjunction with the established rhythm of the music.
Identify and discuss important aspects of modern dance history, tradition, and dance studio etiquette.

rows.title: Intensive Modern Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze anatomical function as it relates to intensive-level dance vocabulary.
Identify intensive-level modern movement sequences integrating dynamic qualities of movement, related to musicality.
Perform intensive-level modern dance sequences that require muscular strength, endurance, flexibility, balance, and coordination.
Identify and discuss in depth important aspects of modern dance history.

rows.title: Advanced Beginning Jazz Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and perform advanced beginning jazz dance vocabulary, combinations, and technique.
Demonstrate correct body alignment both static and dynamic as it applies to advanced beginning jazz dance sequences across the floor.
Identify and perform the techniques of an advanced beginning jazz dance class to build strength and coordination.
Perform advanced beginning jazz movement patterns emphasizing rhythmic structure and syncopation.
Identify and discuss important aspects of jazz dance history.

rows.title: Beginning African-Haitian Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Execute beginning movement vocabulary utilizing various African Haitian technique styles.
Identify and perform basic African Haitian step progressions and choreographies with correct alignment and technique.
Evaluate and perform beginning dance patterns with the appropriate musicality.
Compare dance pioneers and their contributions to African Haitian dance.

rows.title: Beginning Tap Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and apply fundamental movement principles in beginning tap technique.
Demonstrate fundamental tap vocabulary.
Perform drills of fundamental tap vocabulary and beginning combinations with precise musicality.
Discuss the African-American roots of tap dance

rows.title: Beginning Hip Hop Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify beginning-level Hip Hop technique, vocabulary, and combinations.
Perform beginning-level Hip Hop movements in conjunction with the musicality of Hip Hop music and the vocal rhythms.
Explain and demonstrate correct body alignment with beginning isolations and shifting of weight.
Demonstrate coordination, strength, and flexibility to perform beginning-level Hip Hop technique and combinations.
Identify and discuss important aspects of Hip Hop history from 1970 to 1990.

rows.title: Beginning Ballroom Dance
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform beginning level step variations for various ballroom dances.
Analyze posture fundamentals to beginning leading and following techniques, emphasizing correct connection and frame.
Identify musical structure and rhythms for each beginning-level ballroom dance form.
Discuss the historical development of each dance.

rows.title: Beginning Salsa and Other Latin Dances
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform select basic steps, step variations, and movement sequences of Salsa and other Latin American social dances.
Analyze and demonstrate beginning-level leading and following techniques, including frame and connection.
Perform beginning Latin dance steps that align with rhythm and phrasing of the music.
Examine salsa dancing in various cultural, historical, and environmental contexts.

rows.title: Intermediate Argentine Tango
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and use intermediate Argentine Tango movement vocabulary.
Explain intermediate-level frame and connection.
Describe varied styles of Argentine Tango and their defining characteristics.

rows.title: Zumba: Street Style Dance Forms
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform Zumba street-style dance sequences with an emphasis on coordination, spatial patterns, and rhythmic variations.
Explain and demonstrate correct body alignment as it applies to Zumba street-style dance vocabulary, combinations, and technique.
Perform the progressive elements of a Zumba street-style class to increase cardiovascular endurance.
Measure exercise heart rate and monitor pulse rate during recovery phase.

rows.title: Dance Conditioning Level II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the importance of physiologically efficient body alignment as it applies to dance technique.
Perform multi-zone targeting exercises while demonstrating correct body placement and alignment at an advanced beginning level.
Apply anaerobic and aerobic breathing techniques to facilitate advanced beginning-level performance of dance conditioning training.
Demonstrate core strength, flexibility, and stability by targeting multiple muscle groups applying dance conditioning skills and exercises at an advanced beginning level.

rows.title: Dental Materials and Procedures
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify various dental materials and their safe handling.
Apply infection control guidelines in the use of dental materials.
Manipulate various dental materials at a competent level.

rows.title: Dental Roentgenography II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply guidelines of infection control, radiation safety, and quality assurance pertaining to the patient and operator in a dental setting.
Use correct dental radiographic techniques to expose acceptable intraoral and extraoral radiographs.
Apply appropriate patient management techniques when performing dental radiographs.

rows.title: Clinical Dental Assisting Preparation
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create a personal profile for employment opportunities.
Assess solutions to problems in a dental team context.
Perform placement of pit and fissure sealants on patients.

rows.title: Introduction to Medical Radiography
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate the impact of historical events upon the Radiologic Sciences professions.
Describe the sources, properties, and units of measurement for different types of ionizing radiation.
Apply the cardinal principles of radiation protection to the concept of ALARA (as low as reasonably achievable) in a laboratory setting as applicable to clinical practice.
Operate equipment used in the measurement of ionizing radiation.

rows.title: Patient Care in Radiologic Technology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the Radiologic Technologist's scope of practice.
Analyze principles of informed consent, confidentiality, patient rights, and ethical decision-making.
Examine the different approaches to patient care based upon age, gender, religious, and cultural differences.
Demonstrate written and verbal communication skills incorporating medical terminology.

rows.title: Clinical Education in DMI I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Appraise communication models for effectiveness in relating to patients and clinical personnel.
Relate theoretical principles of Diagnostic Medical Imaging to beginning-level clinical performance and practice.
Model optimal professionalism and ethical behavior as it relates to the clinical environment.
Perform clinical procedures according to established competencies of the Diagnostic Medical Imaging program.
Model optimal radiation safety during procedures in a clinical setting.
Model optimal patient care and safety during procedures in a clinical setting.
Solve problems related to radiologic procedures performed and situations encountered in the clinical setting.

rows.title: Clinical Education in DMI III
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Appraise communication models for effectiveness in relating to patients and clinical personnel.
Relate theoretical principles of Diagnostic Medical Imaging to intermediate-advanced level clinical performance and practice.
Model optimal professionalism and ethical behavior as it relates to the clinical environment.
Perform clinical procedures according to established competencies of the Diagnostic Medical Imaging program.
Model optimal radiation safety during procedures in a clinical setting.
Model optimal patient care and safety during procedures in a clinical setting.
Solve problems related to radiologic procedures performed and situations encountered in the clinical setting.

rows.title: Mammography
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Integrate medical terminology into identification of external and internal breast anatomy.
Apply radiation technical factors to mammography quality control and image evaluation.
Compare different treatment methods available for breast pathologies.
Apply information obtained from the patient history, clinical findings, and foundational knowledge of pathophysiology to determine risks for breast cancer.

rows.title: Electrocardiography Professional Practice
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform electrocardiograms on hospital patients in the critical care, emergency department, inpatient, and outpatient settings.
Assist healthcare professionals with preparation and performance of exercise and pharmacologic stress tests.
Integrate electrocardiogram results into the computerized patient archiving system.
Communicate and interact with patients and members of the Non-Invasive Cardiology Department according to standards of the healthcare profession.

rows.title: Advanced Echocardiographic Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the advanced ultrasound imaging modalities and their methods of interrogation in an echocardiographic examination.
Use the cardiac ultrasound systems to perform an exam and interpret findings of 2D and Doppler interrogation of cardiac pathologies.
Analyze the ultrasound images and Doppler finding of normal carotid arteries.
Apply knowledge and skills necessary to pass the national registry examinations.

rows.title: Women in the Economy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain and apply key concepts of gender, social organization, economic systems, and inequality.
Compare typical and changing U.S. household arrangements for the division of domestic labor and relate to individuals’ paid work and well-being.
Evaluate how gender and race-ethnicity shape labor market activities, including issues of occupational segregation and pay inequality.
Analyze the impact of key social movements and government policies on women’s economic activities.
Examine key historical and cultural factors that shape the paid and unpaid work of girls and women in America today.
Apply mainstream economic and political economic theories to the evaluation of gender inequality in the economy today.

rows.title: Principles of Microeconomics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform and interpret microeconomic calculations.
Apply microeconomic models to analyze market outcomes, including market failures and government policies.
Model how consumers and firms make decisions under a variety of market structures.

rows.title: Electronics II: Digital Circuits and Practical Applications
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct combinational and sequential logic circuits using schematics and relevant datasheets.
Troubleshoot digital circuits with modern test equipment.
Design and construct simple electronic projects.
Evaluate voltage and current measurements of a digital circuit with its circuit schematic and block diagram.
Formulate a test procedure to analyze the operation of digital circuits.

rows.title: Electronics IV: Microcontroller Interfaces and Programming
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the basic architecture of a microcontroller based microcomputer system.
Synthesize, integrate, and load driver program into a microcontroller based microcomputer system.
Describe timed events and input and output in a microcontroller-based microcomputer system.
Modify various microcontroller-addressing modes and display results on light emitting diode (LED) ports.

rows.title: National Registry EMT Exam Preparation Course
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the Emergency Medical Technician (EMT) curriculum to answer test items, problem-solve, and respond to emergency situation.
Examine personal health and study habits as they relate to improving performance on the national EMT certifying examination.
Evaluate personal performance on test items within the scope of the EMT curriculum.

rows.title: Trauma Certification
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine EMS trauma care and assessment-based trauma management for adult, pediatric, and geriatric patients.
Apply evidence-based practices to the care of the critical trauma patient according to national trauma standards for advanced level prehospital providers.
Integrate the use of a triage system into the triage of patients and management of the scene at a mass casualty incident.

rows.title: OB/GYN & Pedi Emergencies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform a systematic patient assessment used for evaluating pediatric patients of varying developmental stages.
Determine the most likely etiology of the obstetric and pediatric patient condition using information obtained from patient history, clinical findings, and foundational knowledge of pathophysiology.
Formulate a treatment plan for the obstetric patient, newborn patient, neonate, and pediatric patient in simulated medical and trauma emergencies.
Perform basic and advanced life support management of critical and stable patients with obstetric emergencies within the scope of practice of a paramedic.
Perform basic and advanced life support management of critical and stable pediatric patients within the scope of practice of a paramedic.

rows.title: Writing about Literature
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:

rows.title: Intermediate Fiction Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate choices writers make regarding elements of craft in fiction at an intermediate level.
Compose works of original literary expression, employing, at an intermediate level, elements of craft.
Appraise works-in-progress, sharing substantive critiques with members of a writing workshop in appropriate, constructive ways.
Revise works of literary expression based on instructor feedback and the workshop process.

rows.title: Intermediate Creative Nonfiction Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate how craft choices change meaning in published work and student writing.
Compose works of original literary nonfiction, employing, at an intermediate level, elements of craft.
Appraise works-in-progress, sharing critiques with peers in a workshop setting in appropriate, constructive ways to help the author generate ideas for revision.
Revise works of creative nonfiction based on feedback.

rows.title: Survey of World Literature, Part 1: Ancient, Medieval, and Early Modern
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the major genres, themes, and textual concerns of literature from antiquity through the Renaissance period.
Analyze individual texts in relation to the significant historical, cultural, and/or social issues from antiquity through the Renaissance period.
Analyze the content and formal structures of world literature written from antiquity through the Renaissance period.
Integrate textual evidence and literary criticism when writing essays on key worksfrom antiquity through the Renaissance period.

rows.title: Survey of Literature in English, Part 3: Mid-19th Century to Present
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify the major genres, themes, and textual concerns of literature from the mid-nineteenth century through the present.
Analyze individual texts in relation to the significant historical, cultural, and/or social issues of literature from the mid-nineteenth century through the present.
Analyze the content and formal structures of texts from the mid-nineteenth century through the present.
Integrate textual evidence and literary criticism when writing essays on key works of the mid-nineteenth century through the present.

rows.title: Shakespeare
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the major elements and influences of Elizabethan and Jacobean theaters and conventions of performance.
Analyze individual plays in relation to their form and context.
Analyze specific ways that Shakespeare’s use of language shapes the psychology of characters and themes of the play.
Integrate textual evidence and literary criticism into written analysis of each key play studied.

rows.title: Literature and Film
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe shared themes, narrative structures, and textual concerns in film and literature.
Analyze cinematic and literary methods of story-telling as they relate to critical theory.
Evaluate the relationships between the textual and visual components of cinematic and literary works when arriving at a set of interpretive conclusions.
Integrate textual evidence and both film and literary criticism when writing essays on key works of film and literature.

rows.title: Critical Thinking and Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define, recognize, and utilize forms of critical reasoning, including deductive and inductive reasoning, in a variety of rhetorical contexts.
Reflect critically on one’s own thought processes to identify and avoid cognitive biases and common fallacies of language and thought.
Employ critical reading and research strategies to locate and evaluate complex texts representative of diverse experiences, perspectives, and forms of authority.
Evaluate and document evidence to construct arguments in a variety of rhetorical situations, distinguishing knowledge from belief and fact from judgment.
Draft written arguments to respond appropriately to texts, with attention to intended audience, purpose, and social context, and revise for clarity, cogency, persuasiveness, and soundness.

rows.title: Introduction to Circuit Analysis
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Synthesize a logical, orderly, step-by-step method to determine the natural, forced, and complete responses of zero and higher order linear circuits.
Synthesize a logical, orderly, step-by-step method to determine the currents, voltages, power transfer, and resonance for steady state sinusoidal (AC) circuits and networks.
Categorize basic analog transistor models and Operational Amplifiers configurations.
Configure and manage state-of-the-art computer software tools (spreadsheet, analysis and graphics software tools) to solve circuit problems.

rows.title: Introduction to Clean and Renewable Energy
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Synthesize the basic scientific concepts on which energy resources are grounded.
Summarize the negative impacts and benefits of fossil fuels and other dominant energy resources.
Compare the costs and benefits of energy systems from a scientific, environmental, and policy perspective.
Formulate science-based, evidence-supported arguments and hypotheses on energy-related resource choices and policies.
Evaluate and question claims around energy systems and their environmental impacts.
Calculate energy flows related to consumption and production at macro and micro scales.

rows.title: Social Entrepreneurship
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain social entrepreneurship, its different types, and how it differs from traditional business entrepreneurship.
Build an actionable business model to transform nascent ideas into high-impact social ventures.
Identify systemic global problems and impact metrics to create and measure social impact.
Analyze local and global perspectives and cultural influences that are critical in designing innovative solutions to identified social problem.

rows.title: Applied Research in Sustainability
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply principles and practices of sustainability to project area.
Work collaboratively as a member of a team.
Identify and acquire resources appropriate for assisting with sustainability-related projects.
Apply improved content expertise and acquired professional skills to assess future career goals in the field of sustainability.

rows.title: ESL Listening and Speaking - Low Advanced
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret spoken academic English discourse by applying knowledge of pronunciation features and listening strategies at a low advanced ESL level
Produce comprehensible spoken English in academic contexts incorporating correct pronunciation of segmental and suprasegmental features at a low-advanced ESL level
Assess one's own strengths and areas for improvement to increase accuracy in spoken English at a low-advanced ESL level

rows.title: Introduction to Academic ESL
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use a variety of beginning academic reading and vocabulary development strategies to interpret literary and informational texts.
Compose paragraphs using beginning academic writing strategies, language structures, and vocabulary.
Employ beginning academic listening and speaking strategies to participate in academic settings.
Identify and use college resources to support academic work.

rows.title: Beginning Low 1 Abridged
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret general meaning of low-beginning English conversations on a limited number of familiar topics.
Interpret general meaning of low-beginning English written texts on a limited number of familiar topics.
Produce English at a low-beginning level to communicate orally in a limited number of familiar contexts.
Produce English at a low-beginning level to write simple sentence sentences in a limited number of familiar contexts.

rows.title: Beginning High 3
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify main points in short, simplified spoken texts in English on familiar topics.
Communicate orally in limited familiar social and workplace contexts using a limited range of high-beginning English grammar and vocabulary.
Identify key information in a range of short, simplified written texts in English on familiar topics.
Write simple sentences and short paragraphs about familiar topics using a limited range of high-beginning English grammar and vocabulary.

rows.title: Beginning High 4 Abridged
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret general meaning and some details of high-beginning English oral discourse on a variety of familiar topics.
Interpret general meaning and some details of high-beginning English written discourse on a variety of familiar topics.
Produce English at a high-beginning level to communicate in conversations in a variety of familiar contexts.
Produce English at a high-beginning level to write brief paragraphs in a variety of familiar contexts.

rows.title: Intermediate 5-8 Multilevel
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret main ideas and supporting details in a range of intermediate spoken English texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
Use intermediate language structures and forms to communicate orally in English in a range of contexts
Interpret main ideas and supporting details in a range of intermediate written English texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts
Compose short written texts for a range of purposes
Identify individual language study goals for independent ESL study
Work effectively in a diverse cultural environment at an intermediate level

rows.title: Intermediate High 7 Abridged
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interpret main points and most supporting details in a limited range of high-intermediate adapted and authentic spoken English texts on familiar and unfamiliar topics.
Interpret main points and most supporting details in a limited range of high-intermediate adapted and authentic written English texts on familiar and unfamiliar topics.
Communicate orally in English in extended conversations and discussions, using a limited range of high-intermediate language structures and forms.
Write organized paragraphs with relevant ideas and supporting details, using a limited range of high-intermediate English language structures and forms.

rows.title: Advanced Low 9
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze authentic spoken English texts on a wide variety of complex topics.
Express ideas fluently and accurately in extended discussions, using a range of low-advanced English language structures and vocabulary.
Analyze authentic written English texts on a wide variety of complex topics.
Write cohesive, well-developed multi-paragraph texts using a range of low-advanced English language structures and vocabulary.
Work effectively in a diverse cultural environment at a low-advanced English level.

rows.title: ESL Digital Language Learning
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify individual language study goals for independent ESL study.
Apply strategies for improving English language skills based on assessed needs.
Use digital technologies to access ESL study resources that match identified needs.

rows.title: ESL Projects with Digital Technology - Intermediate
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intermediate-level English language structures and vocabulary to communication in a digital environment.
Identify main ideas and supporting details in intermediate-level adapted texts in familiar and unfamiliar contexts.
Develop intermediate-level English language skills through digital technology procedures and tools.

rows.title: ESL Pronunciation - Intermediate
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply knowledge of the International Phonetic Alphabet to produce the sounds of American English.
Use segmentals and prosodic features to produce comprehensible English at the intermediate language level.
Apply intermediate-level English pronunciation skills in identifying and correcting English pronunciation errors for increased comprehensibility.

rows.title: ESL Beginning Computer Skills - Intro
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use basic terminology to communicate about computers and limited digital processes.
Interpret beginning-level instructions in English to create basic documents, using a variety of tools, including presentation software.
Identify proper keyboarding and posture techniques.

rows.title: ESL for Cooking
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify cooking vocabulary in a restaurant setting using high-beginning English language level.
Apply high-beginning English language skills when communicating about cooking in the restaurant industry.
Apply high-beginning English language skills to the preparation of job search documents and interview answers about cooking in the restaurant industry.

rows.title: ESL Job Search B
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe job qualifications, using appropriate and effective intermediate-level English grammar and vocabulary.

Apply networking and digital literacy skills to gather information about potential employers and proactively market skills and experience using effective intermediate-level English language skills and strategies.
Use intermediate-level English language and communication skills to interview effectively for a specific job.

rows.title: ESL Intermediate Computer Skills C
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intermediate-level English language skills to follow oral and written instructions and create projects using non cloud-based word presentation or spreadsheet software.
Apply appropriate intermediate-level English language and computer skills to deliver a presentation using presentation software and techniques learned in this course.

rows.title: HVAC System Fundamentals
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Calculate air-conditioning cooling loads.
Appraise the efficiency of heat transfer and air handling equipment.
Evaluate the appropriate size and friction pressure drop for ductwork systems.
Estimate fan horsepower from airflow quantity and pressure drop.
Solve steady state AC and DC circuits related to motor sizing and analysis.
Evaluate process control systems and elements related to air conditioning systems.

rows.title: Technical Mathematics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess the most efficient method of vector addition for a particular problem and deconstruct vectors into their components.
Diagram and relate trigonometric functions, logarithmic and exponential functions of any base, radicals, exponents and logs.
Distinguish between different numbering systems.
Synthesize methods of solutions for systems of n equations with n unknowns.
Formulate methods of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division for complex numbers.
Assess best-fit curves to experimental data.

rows.title: Apparel Construction I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Operate sewing machinery properly and safely
Analyze fabric grain and its effect on garment construction
Identify and apply multiple seam finishes, hand and machine stitches, and closures
Construct simple garments

rows.title: Fashion History
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Recognize and evaluate the historical changes in cultures and societies in Western Civilization as evidenced in fashion and other forms of material culture.
Distinguish historical changes through details in the cut and design of clothing, fabric, and accessories.
Identify and evaluate historical influences in contemporary culture and fashion.

rows.title: Fashion Illustration I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the convention of the 10 head proportions to illustrate the fashion figure.
Create a personal style of fashion illustration.
Explore fashion design concepts through fashion illustration.
Communicate fashion designs using a variety of media.

rows.title: Flat Pattern Design II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Comprehend advanced pattern making principles and apply those to create 3D garments from a sketch or picture.
Analyze fit samples on the dress form or fit model and revise patterns to create well-fitting, balanced garments.
Identify appropriate garment fabrications, finishes, and closures.
Generate patterns applicable for use in the industry or manufacturing facility.

rows.title: Visual Merchandising
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the history of visual display and the major retailers that developed the practice.
Define and use visual merchandising terminology appropriately.
Install various types of window and in-store displays and employ a window calendar.
Select and use appropriate props for a given display, and use various equipment and supplies in creating displays.
Explain the role of visual merchandising in a variety of business establishments.

rows.title: Icons of Contemporary Fashion
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply knowledge of the history of dress to creative projects.
Evaluate the historical changes and influences on cultural dress in the United States.
Explain the history and influence of the fashion industry in the United States to the rest of of the world.

rows.title: Fashion Merchandising/Marketing Internship
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Perform assigned essential job tasks under supervision in fashion merchandising, buying, styling, or marketing.
Describe the roles, retail job responsibilities, and organization of the fashion internship business or location
Apply appropriate standards of conduct and personal presentation in the fashion workplace

rows.title: Computerized Pattern Development: Gerber
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
