Create, store, and access digital pattern files using Gerber.
Draft and modify digital pattern blocks to create patterns for original styles using Gerber.
Digitize full-size paper patterns to create digital patterns using Gerber.
Grade styles to achieve multiple sizes using Gerber.

rows.title: Elementary French
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interact orally at the novice mid-level with grammatical accuracy and intelligible pronunciation.
Write descriptively in French using accurate grammar and spelling at the novice mid-level.
Explain short written texts such as social media posts, articles and culture-related materials using structures and vocabulary at the novice mid-level.
Express a cultural awareness of the French-speaking world at the novice mid-level.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary French
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Interact orally at the novice-high level with grammatical accuracy and intelligible pronunciation.
Examine and interpret texts in French at the novice-high level, evaluating such factors as audience, purpose, and communication norms and strategies.
Compose written communications sharing thoughts and opinions in French at a novice-high level.
Express a cultural awareness of the French-speaking world at the novice high-level.

rows.title: Intermediate French
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Express ideas and personal opinions orally using communicative structures in French at an intermediate high-level
Discuss literary and expository texts in French at an intermediate high-level
Produce a cohesive text at a high-intermediate level using the studied structures
Analyze French and francophone cultures through texts, songs, films, and the textbook's cultural notes

rows.title: Physical Geography
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply scientific inquiry and investigation of evidence to critically evaluate physical geography arguments.
Communicate scientific ideas and theories about physical geography effectively.
Apply scientific principles, theories, or models to explain the behavior of physical geography phenomena.
Apply physical geographic knowledge and reasoning to human interaction with the natural world.

rows.title: Physical Geography Laboratory
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Investigate natural phenomena through a variety of scientific inquiry techniques associated with physical geography.
Analyze and evaluate physical geographic data from the natural world.
Apply scientific principles, theories, or models associated with physical geography to predict and explain the behavior of natural phenomena.

rows.title: Economic Geography
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate the validity and applicability of economic geography location models.
Summarize the spatial social patterns of modern cities through the organization of urban economies.
Analyze the economic impact of globalization of the economy on the geography of the modern world.

rows.title: Historical Geology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply scientific inquiry and the investigation of evidence to critically evaluate scientific arguments relating to historical geology.
Communicate historical geology ideas and theories effectively.
Apply geologic, stratigraphic, and fossil principles, theories, or models to interpret ancient environments, paleoclimates, and plate tectonic settings.
Evaluate the ways in which historical geology principles and data impact society and how living organisms have impacted and continue to impact Earth's history.

rows.title: San Francisco Geology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Observe, describe, and analyze the physical forces and processes that have shaped the major topographical features found within the city of San Francisco.
Collect and analyze rock, sediment, soil, and fossil samples and use them to develop working hypotheses about local geologic processes.
Evaluate geologic hazards within San Francisco, and identify and evaluate what has been done to minimize their damage.
Review and evaluate the supporting data for the geological history of San Francisco.

rows.title: Essential Skills for Business Professionals
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply professional workforce protocols in behavior in a business environment.
Apply a range of professional skills to solve workplace issues.
Collaborate effectively in teams and across different cultures.
Communicate professionally using verbal means, non-verbal means, and in writing.

rows.title: Introduction to Health Care
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine the history of medicine, the current health care delivery system, and community services in the United States.
Analyze types of patient records from a variety of health care delivery areas.
Examine the characteristics of numbering systems, and apply these principles to various numbering systems and storage methodology.
Discuss the career and educational pathways available for Medical Assisting and Health Information Technology.
Distinguish among computerized patient records, electronic medical records, and electronic health records.

rows.title: The United States Since 1900
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply appropriate methods of inquiry when analyzing and synthesizing historical evidence and interpretations of United States History since 1900.
Examine artistic and cultural traditions in their historical context in the history of the United States since 1900.

Explain the impact of industrialization, urbanization, unionism, immigration, and the intellectual, cultural, racial, gender, and class underpinnings of American society in the late 1890s and twentieth and twenty-first centuries in the United States.
Evaluate the major social, technological, scientific, political, and economic developments in United States history since 1900, their causes and effects and their historical significance.
Analyze the United States within a global context that also includes non-Western countries in history since 1900.
Interpret primary and secondary sources to be integrated as support in a written analysis of United States History since 1900.

rows.title: History of Latin America Since Independence
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Recognize and apply the different methods of inquiry used in the social sciences to study Latin American history.
Compare the different struggles for independence throughout Latin America during the long 19th century
Explain the emergence of elite-led political, social, cultural and economic systems in the 19th century and the consequences for Latin American societies.
Analyze the economic models, political systems, cultural tensions and social revolutions present in the 20th and 21st-century experiences of Latin Americans.
Synthesize historical primary sources and existing secondary interpretations to create analytical narratives about the Latin American past.

rows.title: History of the Philippines
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze major migration theories and material evidence of human culture and society in the archipelago prior to Spanish colonization.
Compare the motives and policies of the colonial powers that entered the Philippines and their impact on the culture and people.
Evaluate the arguments for independence and resistance through each period of colonization.
Interpret the policies of the Philippines after independence from the United States, including Martial Law and post-Martial law period.
Evaluate and synthesize historical evidence and interpretations drawn from both primary and secondary sources as related to the history of the Philippines.

rows.title: LGBT United States History
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the major transformations of LGBT movements that occurred from the 1950s onward as a result of new ethnic, feminist, and organizational concerns.
Discuss and evaluate the existence and contributions of lesbians, gay men, bisexual, and transgender people throughout the history of the United States and the strategies they used for survival.
Identify the major personalities, groups, and events involved in the lesbian/gay/bisexual/transgender movements for social change and the basic programs of reforms proposed.
Analyze and evaluate the development of lesbian, gay, bisexual, and transgender identities and communities in the 20th/21st century.

rows.title: Europe Since 1900
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate and synthesize historical evidence and interpretations by using methods of inquiry and expression appropriate to the study of Europe since 1900.
Interpret primary and secondary sources to be integrated as support in a written argument or interpretation of topics covering Europe since 1900.
Evaluate the impact of a wide breadth of societal trends and changes related to Europe since 1900.
Explain the major technological and scientific developments in the history of Europe since 1900, their causes and effects, and their historical significance.
Examine artistic and cultural traditions in their historical context in the history of Europe since 1900.
Analyze Europe since 1900 within a global context that also includes non-European countries.

rows.title: Medical Terminology I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define the roots, prefixes, and suffixes used in medical terminology and apply the rules to form and define medical terms.
Construct medical terms from definitions of medical conditions and procedures.
Interpret medical abbreviations from patient case studies and reports.
Integrate the application of medical terminology into the anatomy, diseases, symptoms, laboratory data, and pharmaceuticals for selected body systems.
Interpret the medical terminology found in patient case histories, operative reports, discharge summaries, and special procedures.

rows.title: Organization of Health Data
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze hospital institutional data in relation to regulatory and accreditation standards.
Explain the sources of health data, types of health data and the requirements for various data sets and databases.
Describe uses of registry data for educational, administrative, and research purposes.
Use appropriate quantitative and qualitative methodologies to collect and analyze statistical data related to patient care and services.
Apply data to administrative decisions and problem solving.

rows.title: Organization and Management in Health
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare various management theories and functions and how they are utilized in a health care environment.
Describe various planning and management tools and communication processes used in health care environments.
Identify the quality improvement techniques used in health care.
Identify the steps involved in the staffing, selection, training, and evaluation of healthcare employees.
Explain how morale, discipline, and differences influence the healthcare environment.

rows.title: Healthcare Quality and Reimbursement
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the historical development of quality improvement measures, healthcare reimbursement and payment systems, and the evolution of value-based-purchasing/pay-for-performance.

Analyze quality improvement programs, coding compliance issues related to clinical outcomes measures, and reimbursement methodologies according to accrediting agency standards, government regulations, and institutional needs.
Collect, organize, and analyze healthcare data for quality, utilization, risk management, reimbursement trends, and other facility operations.
Evaluate a complete health care cycle and identify clinical and financial performance improvement opportunities.
Apply the fundamentals of team leadership and communication tools used in performance improvement and revenue cycle activities.

rows.title: Community and Group Forums
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Implement administrative functions and activity planning, including the actions necessary to start, maintain, and evaluate a group.
Organize and prepare a community assessment plan based on wellness and recovery principles.
Evaluate and apply wellness and recovery, strength-based facilitation strategies in diverse groups and behavioral health settings.
Execute behavioral health, psycho-educational, and wellness and recovery groups across the life span.

rows.title: Health Impacts of Incarceration
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the historical, political and economic development of the U.S. criminal justice system and its effects on public health and health inequalities.
Examine the health impacts of incarceration and the social and systemic barriers upon reentry for individuals, families, and communities.
Compare alternative criminal justice models and reentry programs that promote positive health outcomes for formerly incarcerated populations.
Analyze the role of frontline advocates and social and health workers, and the strategies and skills for promoting the health and well being of formerly incarcerated populations.

rows.title: Children's Healthy Eating & Nutrition
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine the relationship between child growth and development and nutritional needs and eating behaviors
Assess dietary adequacy using appropriate food guidance systems and current dietary guidelines to promote and maintain health.
Analyze the impact of food security and health disparities on families to increase access to nutritious and affordable food.
Apply basic food management and safe handling skills to plan and create simple and healthy meals and snacks.
Plan, conduct, and evaluate effective techniques and resources for providing age appropriate nutrition education to youth.

rows.title: CHW Internship Placement
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the roles, job responsibilities, and organization of the community health internship program or institution.
Perform assigned essential job tasks under supervision in the community health field.
Apply appropriate standards of ethical and professional conduct in the community health workplace.

rows.title: Women, Health, and Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intersectional feminist theory to understand the forces that shape women's health outcomes and policies

Analyze how social determinants of health, including physical, psychological, environmental, and social aspects, affect the risk factors, prevention, treatment, and quality of health services for diverse communities of women using evidence-based research.
Analyze behavior change theories and models as they relate to community and public health efforts.
Evaluate qualitative and quantitative women's health research to gain an understanding of scientific validity, ethical issues, and potential cultural and demographic bias.
Describe sexual anatomy and physiology, sexual response, reproductive health and justice, and sexually transmitted infection prevention.
Examine contemporary health issues and ethics, including body image, gender role and expression, ageism, and violence prevention.

rows.title: Introduction to Health and Well-Being
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze factors, including personal behaviors and social determinants, which influence health and illness within a health equity framework
Assess prevention, treatment, health promotion, and advocacy strategies to enhance health and well-being and address common health behaviors and conditions
Examine the US healthcare system, consumer rights and strategies to access services to improve health.
Evaluate health information and resources to support health and well-being

rows.title: Critical Perspectives in Global Health
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze definitions of global health and key indicators used to asses global health status
Analyze the multiple factors that influence and determine global health and inequalities among populations and nations
Assess the burden of disease in various regions of the world, including variation within and across countries, demographic and racial/ethnic populations
Examine the relationship between education, socioeconomic status, equity and population health status within and among countries

Analyze ethical and human rights concerns, particularly access to basic human needs, health services, and medicines, and the responses to critical needs after a natural and/or human-generated disaster
Analyze policy and program approaches to prioritizing and addressing global health issues and strategies that strengthen community capabilities to enable health and well-being

rows.title: Facilitating Trainings in Community & Public Health
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and describe the major components of public health education.
Design community and public health education trainings on topics relevant to the work of community health workers.
Plan and facilitate health education trainings to meet learning objectives applicable to the community health worker field.

rows.title: Physiological Effects of Addiction
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the structure and operation of the nervous system and other organs of the body and how psychoactive substances affect the operation of these systems
Analyze the behavioral, psychological and physiological effects of psychoactive and other drugs on the human body and human behavior
Compare different pharmacological treatments, their implications and interventions for substance use disorders, mental health, and dual conditions
Analyze evidence-based literature and peer-reviewed journals on impact of trauma on brain chemistry and best practices for addiction disorders and interventions

rows.title: Interpreting in Healthcare I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply standards, protocols, and skills in managing basic to moderate levels of interpreting encounters.
Research disease processes and cultural implications at an introductory level.
Compare various biomedical cultures and cultural-specific health beliefs and practices.
Explain the role of a healthcare interpreter.
Employ job readiness skills, from social presence to collaborative teamwork.

rows.title: Professional Skills for Healthcare Interpreters
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe challenges in special populations and explain strategies to promote health equity.
Articulate language access laws, regulations, and accreditation standards.
Analyze job opportunities and self-assess readiness.

rows.title: How Trauma Affects Our Lives
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze common causes of and responses to trauma.
Identify common approaches and local resources for promoting recovery from trauma.

rows.title: Mindful Stress Reduction
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate mindfulness practices for personal stress reduction
Select and practice appropriate stress reduction techniques

rows.title: Treatment Modalities in Addiction Recovery
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the Diagnostic Statistical Manual (DSM)-5 criteria for and the various treatment models used in substance use and co-occurring disorder treatment.
Asses and integrate stages of change theory, fluctuating motivation and resistance within treatment planning and intervention.
Examine and demonstrate competency in multidimensinal assessment and case conceptionalization to develop appropriate treatment plans for clients with substance use disorders.
Apply evidence-based treatment strategies, their benefits and challenges within the continuum of care to support recovery and relapse prevention in a range of treatment settings.
Integrate culturally responsive and client-centered approaches to ensure ethical and personalized treatment planning for diverse populations in treatment counseling.

rows.title: Bay Area Arts
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify artists who have left their mark on the Bay Area's cultural landscape as well as the aesthetic characteristics of their work.
Analyze artists' works in the context of Bay Area history.
Distinguish among the artistic contributions of various regions of the Bay Area and San Francisco neighborhoods.
Apply an intercultural appreciation of aesthetics to the study of Bay Area artworks.

rows.title: Philosophies of Religion
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify core concepts of the course's religions as represented in their sacred texts.
Compare the world views shown in sacred texts.
Analyze sacred texts.

rows.title: Islam: Identity & Culture
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare the origins, foundational principles and practices of Islam with those of other major religions.
Evaluate major differences among historical and current Muslim groups, including American Muslims.
Analyze gender equity and disparity in Muslim texts.
Assess the scientific and cultural contributions of Muslims.
Analyze representations of Islam and Muslims in the media and popular culture.

rows.title: Women and Gender in the Middle East
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the impact of religious and cultural gender norms in relation to women’s lives in the Middle East/SWANA.
Assess the diversity of Middle Eastern/SWANA women's experience in relation to social, historical, and geographical context.
Evaluate Western perspectives on Middle Eastern/SWANA women historically and currently.
Compare political and social movements in the SWANA/Middle East region as relates to gender issues over time using social science methodologies.
Analyze contributions that SWANA/Middle Eastern women have made in artistic and intellectual production.

rows.title: Pacific Islanders in the United States
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe the diversity of the Pacific Islander and Oceania communities in the United States and beyond.
Implement indigenous research methodologies used in the study of peoples from the Pacific Islands and Oceania.
Examine the impact and histories of immigration, migration, colonization, and diaspora in the shaping of Pacific Islander & Oceania ethnic and racial formations in the United States.
Appraise and create Pacific Islander and Oceania artistic and cultural representations that speak to race and ethnicity in the United States.
Analyze the relationship between culture, power, knowledge, and decolonization in shaping Pacific Islander identities.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Sexism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze sexism as a system of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes in relation to sexism.
Examine individual and collective ways of taking action against sexism.
Explain the intersectionality of sexism with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Diversity and Social Justice: Transphobia
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and analyze transphobia as a system of oppression and privilege.
Assess biases and stereotypes regarding transphobia.
Examine individual and collective ways of taking action against transphobia.
Explain the intersectionality of transphobia with other distinct forms of social oppression.

rows.title: Interior Design Studio I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Create interior design solutions in response to programming, space planning and circulation
Evaluate a proposed interiors solution against project requirements
Analyze and communicate design process visually, orally, in writing, and in models (hand and digital)
Research and select appropriate materials and specifications for function and aesthetic values

rows.title: Beginning Conversational Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply intelligible pronunciation and intonation at an intermediate-low level when narrating in the present or past
Communicate using accurate grammatical structures in Italian at intermediate-low level to describe daily routines, reciprocal actions, and speak about past events

Respond effectively to spoken Italian with appropriate grammatical forms, accurate vocabulary, and clear pronunciation at an intermediate-low level demonstrating an understanding of human interactions
Compare aspects of Italian culture and geography related to fashion, cuisine, technology, and regions

rows.title: Elementary Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally using present and past tense syntax at a beginning level in Italian.
Read and write in Italian at a beginning level.
Apply clear Italian pronunciation and intonation when responding to spoken Italian at a beginning level.
Explain elements of Italian culture at a level appropriate for a beginning-level Italian language learner.

rows.title: Intermediate Italian
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate in Italian at an intermediate level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation, and clear intonation.
Interpret the main idea of a written text in Italian at an intermediate level.
Analyze and compose short written communications in Italian at an intermediate level.
Assess and articulate aspects of Italian culture responsively at an intermediate level.

rows.title: Continuation of Beginning Conversational Japanese
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally at an advanced beginning level in Japanese
Explain elements of Japanese culture at an advanced beginning level

rows.title: Intermediate Kanji for Reading and Writing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Comprehend the meaning of approximately 200 single characters at an intermediate level and apply that knowledge to the meaning of compound characters
Identify pronunciation of kanji with phonetic elements at an intermediate level
Identify and interpret kanji’s root meaning based on radicals at an intermediate level
Analyze authentic reading materials that contain kanji at an intermediate level
Compose short essays by selecting appropriate kanji at an intermediate level

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Japanese Part I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Japanese at a pre-advanced beginning level.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a pre-advanced beginning level.
Compose short communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a pre-advanced beginning level.
Explain basic elements of Japanese culture.

rows.title: Intermediate Japanese Part I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally at a pre-basic intermediate level in Japanese.
Interpret the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a pre-basic intermediate level.
Compose short communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a pre-basic intermediate level.
Discuss essential elements of Japanese culture.

rows.title: Continuation of Intermediate Japanese Part II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Japanese at a mid-intermediate level.
Analyze the main ideas and grammatical forms of a written text in Japanese at a mid intermediate level.
Create written communications in the Japanese syllabic writing systems and Kanji at a mid-intermediate level.
Evaluate elements of Japanese culture in relation to diverse communication practices.

rows.title: Copy Editing
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and assess the characteristics of a good copy editor.
Use accepted Associated Press style.
Summarize the key ingredients of a news and feature story.
Identify and correct English language usage errors.
Produce headlines suitable for publication in a mass-circulated newspaper, magazine, or news website.

rows.title: Introduction to Magazine Editing and Production
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the various types of writing, editing, photography, illustration and/or design that go into producing a magazine.
Create written, photographic, illustration or design content for a magazine at an introductory level.
Identify and summarize the basic principles and practices that go into producing a magazine.

rows.title: Introduction to Photojournalism
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Collaborate with department editors to organize photographic assignments.
Create aesthetically appealing compositions using various creative tools and camera techniques.
Integrate photographic skills using digital editing techniques and related computer programs and equipment.
Apply skills to create and maintain a portfolio of photojournalism images.
Explain the role of the photojournalist and their work in the field of journalism.

rows.title: Drug Wars in the Americas
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish the historical and political context that led to the emergence of licit and illicit drugs in the United States and Latin America.
Compare past and present drug reduction and control policies implemented in the war against drugs.
Assess the impact of the United States' political, social, and economic influence in shaping drug laws and drug policy initiatives in Latin America.
Evaluate the impact of the drug wars on democracy, rule of law and civil society in Latin America and the United States.
Appraise the complexity of organized crime, insurgency and terrorism in Latin America and their reliance on the production and sale of illicit drugs to the United States.

rows.title: Critical Thinking in Latinx Studies
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply theory and knowledge produced by Latinxs and other people of color to critique rhetorical works focused on Latinxs.
Assess U.S. media and popular culture texts for their use of common narratives, stereotypes, or tropes regarding Latinxs, and juxtapose these with Latin American media.
Analyze and interpret the roles that racialization, ethnicity, and white supremacy play in aspects of Latinx experience as represented in popular discourses in the U.S.

Analyze critically through written works the intersection of race and racism as applied to dimensions of difference common to Latinxs in the U.S., including class, national origins, and immigration status.

rows.title: Shaping Public Policy for Labor and Community Organizations
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess the role of powerful individuals and groups in determining policies that affect working people on the job and in the diverse communities where they live.
Apply various theories and methods of how labor and community organizations influence the policy process to benefit their members and larger communities.
Assess state, federal, and international conditions as they influence public policy choices facing local governments.
Analyze written public policy on subjects of importance to diverse labor and community organizations.
Create a portfolio of public policy advocacy documents.

rows.title: Who Built America? From Reconstruction to the Present
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define the main developments in U.S. labor and working class history from the post-Civil War Reconstruction Era to the present.
Evaluate how the interactions between the working class, including organized labor, and other main social classes in the U.S. shaped the country from 1870 to today.
Identify the ways in which unions and workers' racial, ethnic, migration, and immigration status have influenced U.S. society and culture.
Analyze the organizations developed by working people to advance their interests, including the workers' civil rights or labor union movement.
Evaluate the relevance of U.S. labor and working class history to key social trends today.

rows.title: LGBT Culture & Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare LGBTQ+ social justice movements within the context of other social justice movements.
Analyze intersecting identities and problems with identity politics.
Interpret LGBTQ+ culture and society within decolonial contexts.
Analyze social investment in maintaining binaries.

rows.title: Transgender Lives, Culture and Art
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Examine the cultural, political, and social contexts within which transgender, non-binary, and gender diverse individuals have lived and created art and literature.

rows.title: Modern Physics for Scientists and Engineers
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate concepts, processes, and results from physics effectively.
Apply the fundamental laws of modem physics to investigate and assess physical phenomena that impact society.
Use mathematics up to and including calculus to solve modem physics problems.

rows.title: Ethnic Politics in the United States
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the relationship between racial/ethnic identity and politics.

Compare the political experience, organization, and participatory behavior at least three of African-Americans, Latino/Hispanic Americans, Asian-Americans, Indigenous/First Nations Americans and European-Americans.
Utilize diverse political theoretical approaches to understand ethnic politics, including liberalism/pluralism, conservatism, socialism, and post-modern theories.
Discuss the salient policy issues that affect and direct ethnic political activity.
Analyze multiracial politics and identity.

rows.title: Comparative Government
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate texts and ideas in the field of Comparative Politics.
Apply the comparative method to identifying and explaining similarities and differences among various political thoughts and actions throughout the world.
Compare a variety of political and political economic systems, both in theory and with country examples.
Distinguish among regime types and their central features, with a focus on democratic regimes
Explain the impact of the regional, environmental, economic, historical and cultural factors on political behavior and institutions.

rows.title: Independent Studies in Political Science
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and discuss topics under consideration in the individual political science study.
Utilize social sciences research methods and primary and secondary sources to develop an argument or interpretation.

rows.title: American Government and Politics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain the founding and development of the U.S. and California Constitution.
Critique governing institutions and political processes within the United States and California.
Employ introductory political science research methods to contextualize contemporary political issues and operations in the United States and California.
Assess civil liberties and civil rights of individuals and groups as articulated in the U.S. and California Constitutions and subsequent court decisions.
Investigate the role of identity and political ideology in shaping public opinion and public policy in the United States and California.
Analyze how to effectively participate in politics at the national, state, county, and/or city levels.

rows.title: Assertive Behavior
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Differentiate between assertive, aggressive, passive, and passive-aggressive behavior.
Identify psychological and emotional barriers to assertive behavior.
Describe the psychological effects of socialization, gender, and culture on assertiveness and how assertiveness is viewed.
Apply cognitive-behavioral psychology techniques and strategies for overcoming barriers to assertive behavior.

rows.title: Lifespan Development
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Compare major theoretical perspectives used to explain human development from conception through death.
Explain the primary developmental tasks associated with different periods of the lifespan.
Analyze the interaction of different areas of development and how such interaction affects developmental outcomes.
Evaluate the effects of the multiple and diverse contexts in which development occurs.
Apply developmental concepts, theories, and research findings to the developing person.

rows.title: Applied Psychology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe key psychological concepts, theories, and research findings relevant to human adjustment.
Apply psychological principles that can facilitate and support personal human adjustment in various life contexts and experiences.
Analyze strategies and interventions that can facilitate psychological adjustment and address common adjustment challenges.
Evaluate the impact of sociocultural forces on individual psychological adjustment and overall emotional well-being.

rows.title: Statistics for Behavioral Sciences
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply statistical concepts and describe how they affect the interpretation of specific analyses, including interpreting the statistical significance of p values.
Utilize calculators and/or computer software to perform various statistical tests.
Analyze the strengths and weaknesses of research findings given how data is collected and analyzed in the behavioral sciences.
Assess statistical analysis for appropriateness given the level or scale of measurement of a variable.
Distinguish between experimental and correlational methods in terms of their respective assumptions, interpretations, and limitations in the behavioral sciences.

Use appropriate statistical techniques to analyze and interpret applications based on data from behavioral sciences, economics, social science, psychology, political science, administration of justice, life science, physical science, health science, education and other related fields.

rows.title: Fire Safety Director
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Define the role and responsibilities of the Fire Safety Director position
Define what qualifies as a high rise building and what occupancies require a Fire Safety Director as required by law
Perform required evolutions for emergency evacuation for relocation in a high-rise building

Train members of the emergency response team and floor warden organization in the identification and use of facility fire safety equipment; evacuation needs of the physically disabled; emergency communications, and appropriate actions to be taken during emergencies

rows.title: Conceptual Physical Science
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Evaluate physical science arguments in a critical manner through the application of scientific inquiry and investigation of evidence.
Communicate scientific ideas and theories effectively.
Explain the behavior of natural physical phenomena through the application of scientific principles, theories, or models.
Apply physical science knowledge and reasoning to human interaction with the natural world and issues impacting society.

rows.title: Incident Command System ICS 400: Advanced ICS Command and General Staff-Complex Incidents
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explain how major incidents pose special management challenges and demonstrate how to organize and manage those incidents.
Describe the circumstances in which an area command is established and show how to organize and manage these incidents.
Describe with examples the circumstances in which multi-agency coordination systems are established.

rows.title: Introduction to Fire Science
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and explain the use of fire service equipment and apparatuses and how they are used in fire suppression operations.
Describe fire service organizational structures, Incident Command Systems (ICS), and communication systems that support the fire service organization.
Evaluate operational and training safety practices that focus on firefighter health and safety.
Explain fire dynamics and their effects in fire incidents as related to firefighting operations.
Compare fire prevention, fire investigation, medical services and other specialty fire service programs designed to protect the public.

rows.title: Wildland Fire Control
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify fuels, topography, weather, and fire behavior as they relate to wildland fire incidents
Explain the various approaches to control and extinguish wildland fires
Describe specific safety considerations connected with wildland firefighting such as personnel safety, fire behavior, and proper use of equipment and tools
Compare the factors affecting wildland fires with the recognized tactics employed to extinguish wildland fires

rows.title: Vehicle Extrication
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Assess a vehicle accident scene utilizing safety considerations and the use of the Incident Command System (ICS)
Evaluate vehicle stabilization techniques, vehicle access and egress, rescue access and egress options for a vehicle accident
Remove victims to a safe area using vehicle extrication tools and equipment

rows.title: Company Officer 2B: General Administrative Functions
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Articulate state and federal laws and regulations pertaining to fire service supervisors and the risks of civil and criminal liability for violations of these rules.
Formulate the purpose of each management component of the organization.
Devise a budget and purchasing process that complies with local governmental guidelines.
Describe the need for collecting incident-response data that is accurate and timely to determine incident trending.

rows.title: Instructor I - State Fire Trng
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ the Four-Step Method of Vocational Instruction to provide instruction in fire training principles.
Analyze an existing lesson plan and adapt it to present an effective psychomotor or technical lesson.
Organize the educational environment so that it is conducive to learning.
Produce peer feedback to student instructors that encourages positive instructional techniques and identifies aspects that need improvement.
Administer oral, written, and performance exams in a manner that eliminates bias and discrimination, follows correct procedures, and maintains security of test materials.

rows.title: Social Work Practicum
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply the major components of social work and human services to a practice setting.

Apply knowledge of the National Association of Social Work (NASW) Code of Ethics, fundamental legal guidelines, privacy, and information management related to professional practice within specific agency settings.
Demonstrate personal self-awareness, the practice of non-judgmental assessment, cultural engagement, and support capability.
Demonstrate professional development through the incorporation of feedback from supervision.

rows.title: Social Problems
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Articulate major problems affecting society employing a sociological perspective.
Integrate sociological theories and concepts to explore the social construction of social problems.
Analyze quantitative and qualitative data to determine the consequences of social problems.
Analyze actions that address social problems using sociological approaches.

rows.title: Race, Ethnicity, and Society
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze how race and ethnicity, as social institutions and critical ethnic studies concepts, organize social life across multiple dimensions.
Illustrate the specific mechanisms by which categories and ideas of race and ethnicity are constructed through lived experiences, policies, cultural practices, and representations.

Apply theories and frameworks from the disciplines of Sociology and Ethnic Studies to the lived experiences and social struggles of African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and/or Latino/a Americans in order to analyze and reframe topical contemporary discussions about racial-ethnic identity and racism.

Evaluate social scientific data on African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and/or Latino/a Americans concerning various forms of racial and ethnic prejudice, discrimination, and privilege to develop sociological and ethnic studies explanations for their causes and impacts.

Articulate the ways that knowledge produced by African Americans, Native Americans, Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders, and/or Latino/a American communities have engaged with race and ethnicity as symbols across multiple social institutions with the goals of establishing sovereignty, equality and racial justice.

rows.title: Intermediate Conversational Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Express ideas and opinions effectively in Spanish at an intermediate level with accurate grammatical structure, intelligible pronunciation.
Use accurate grammatical structures in Spanish at an intermediate level to express wishes, subjective reactions, uncertainty and personal opinions.
Interpret spoken Spanish at an intermediate level when presented with present, past or future events, in hypothetical or subjective situations.

Compare socioeconomic and cultural differences between Latin American and Spanish Peninsular cultures in the context of racial and social diversity, artistic expressions, migrations, and environmental impacts of climate change.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Spanish at a mid-intermediate level with accurate grammatical structures, intelligible pronunciation, and clear intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at a mid-intermediate level.
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of Spanish grammar and syntax at a mid-intermediate level.
Compare aspects of Latin America and Spanish Peninsular cultures and societies.

rows.title: Continuation of Elementary Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate orally in Spanish at a low-intermediate level with accurate grammatical structures, intelligible pronunciation, and intonation.
Interpret the main ideas of a written text in Spanish at an intermediate low level.
Compose short written communications incorporating the principles of Spanish grammar and syntax at an intermediate low level.
Compare aspects of Latin America and Spanish Peninsular cultures and societies.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 1A
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the grammar and syntax structures of language, assessing differences between formal and informal registers.
Produce written pieces utilizing accurate grammar, structure and enriched vocabulary, while avoiding literal translation and interference from English.
Communicate effectively using an enriched vocabulary as well as different registers of the language, and identify the significance these registers have in the professional world.
Analyze new perspectives of the diverse cultures of the Spanish-speaking world under a wide historical, artistic, and social background.

rows.title: Spanish for Heritage Speakers 2B
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze and synthesize Spanish grammar structures and syntax rules using linguistic knowledge to infer spelling, time frames, and sentence construction.

Communicate in writing with enriched Spanish vocabulary and complex syntax producing full paragraphs that are organized and detailed, providing a well-supported argument, without interference with English.
Express thoughts efficiently on topics of personal and community interest using a broad range of vocabulary and high-frequency structures.
Compare cultural aspects of Spanish-speaking countries of the Andean and Southern Cone regions.

rows.title: Advanced Spanish: Hispanic Culture and Civilization
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Communicate effectively in Spanish about Hispanic cultures.
Analyze critically significant issues of each chronological period of Hispanic civilization from the beginning of its history through the 17th century.
Identify historical figures and moments of the Hispanic cultures and civilization from the beginning of its history through the 17th century.
Compare Spanish, Hispanic American, and Hispanic cultures from the beginning of its history through the 17th century.

rows.title: Intro to Literature in Spanish
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze a literary passage in terms of style and content and within a cultural context.
Integrate and apply new vocabulary and introductory concepts of literary criticism and literary history in the interpretation of Spanish literature.
Compare literary movements and authors within the larger context of Hispanic cultures and literature.
Identify and explain the distinctive components of literary genres produced in Spanish-speaking cultures and how each one conveys a message in a different manner.

rows.title: Custodial Training for Healthcare Workers
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Identify and assess the health risks related to custodial work in the healthcare industry.
Apply industry-standard techniques and approved procedures while cleaning healthcare sites and disposing of waste.
Explain patients' rights and interface with them appropriately.

rows.title: Design Thinking
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Use design thinking as a mindset and a process.
Identify the drivers and barriers to design thinking.
Apply strategies to develop design solutions.

rows.title: Color in Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Explore, describe and differentiate the color models, processes and materials used with the various fields of design.
Utilize colors and color harmonies in formal compositions produced with both analog and digital tools.
Analyze and compare the historical, cultural, psychological, symbolic and personal uses of color in their own design work and the work of others.
Employ an iterative design process in individual and collaborative design activities.

rows.title: Package Design
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Discuss the function of package design in advertising communication.
Identify the target market and evaluate its role in relationship to design solutions.
Apply and demonstrate compositional skills working with type, color, pattern and 3-dimensional form in building comps and models.
Employ critical thinking and communication skills in the development of package design solutions, using relevant concepts and terminology.
Employ and document an iterative design process.

rows.title: Typography II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ aspects of fine typography for screen and print.
Select appropriate typefaces, font formats and digital tools for screen and print typography.
Discuss historical and contemporary classification, typefaces, designers, and foundries.
Use an iterative design process to solve communication problems, working both individually and collaboratively.
Critique the merits of various design solutions using design and type terminology and concepts.

rows.title: Illustrator II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct complex Illustrator files using industry-standard best practices and advanced features.
Integrate artwork from Adobe Illustrator into other image-creation software.
Employ an iterative process when producing original work.
Assess design solutions and articulate their strengths and weaknesses.

rows.title: Photoshop II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Construct complex Photoshop files using industry-standard best practices and advanced features.
Analyze and reproduce complex Photoshop files using appropriate tools and techniques.
Use an iterative design process to create professional-level digital artwork using Adobe Photoshop.
Assess design solutions and articulate their strengths and weaknesses.

rows.title: Digital Illustration II
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Research a topic thoroughly for the purpose of creating an illustration.
Create a narrative sequence of illustrations.
Collaborate to generate concepts and realize them visually.
Conceptualize and produce characters for use in a narrative (animation, graphic novel, children's book).

rows.title: Design Studio Practicum I
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Employ a structured design process incorporating peer and instructor feedback.
Combine appropriate aesthetic form and content to create engaging and effective communication design.
Demonstrate design and production documentation skills such as time tracking, project summaries, and style guides.

rows.title: Nurse Assistant/Acute Care
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Summarize the role of the certified nursing assistant in the acute care setting.
Compare patient needs and appropriate nursing care in long-term and acute care settings.
Apply proper techniques when performing a range of patient care skills in an acute care setting.

Evaluate and provide appropriate patient care for a range of patients found in an acute care setting, including patients with diabetes, cancer, postoperative patients, and patients with problems of the nervous, circulatory, or respiratory system.
Explain the responsibilities of a certified nursing assistant with regards to wound care in an acute care setting.

rows.title: Pharmacology
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Calculate basic mathematical problems involving fractions, decimals, percentages, and ratios.
Apply the principles of medication administration, including the safe administration of drugs, in caring for clients in various types of clinical settings.
Describe the common classifications, dosages, side effects, and potential adverse reactions of drugs used for the different body systems.
Differentiate the actions and side effects of commonly prescribed medications, including evaluation of the effectiveness of the drugs administered.
Summarize the legal implications associated with medication administration.
Plan appropriate nursing care in administering medications, considering the genetic differences and cultural backgrounds of diverse clients.

rows.title: Maternity and Pediatrics
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Describe and discuss prenatal care, adaptations to pregnancy, and fetal development and reproductive health issues.
Discuss prenatal, antepartum, and postpartum nursing care, including the risks, complications, and nursing interventions.
Describe the physiology of the different systems of the body and age-appropriate assessment, diagnostic tests, and pediatric diseases affiliated with those systems.
Employ critical thinking and appropriate clinical judgment when identifying and describing nursing responsibilities and interventions for hospitalized children from infancy to adolescence.
Explain the responsibility of vocational nurses to report necessary notifiable diseases and/or conditions to public health authorities.
Discuss cultural differences and their influence on childbirth and the family unit.

rows.title: Women and Film
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Apply fundamental terms from foundational feminist film studies.
Analyze female representation from the silent era to today.
Assess film genres, focused on those with potential to challenge traditional gender roles, including comedy and melodrama.
Interpret the work of significant independent, diverse, feminist filmmakers that challenges mainstream representations of women.

rows.title: The Politics of Sexual Violence
rows.heading: STUDENT LEARNING OUTCOMES
rows.lead: Upon completion of this course, a student will be able to:
outcomes: Analyze the political, social, and psychological causes of sexual violence, which disproportionately affects women
Analyze the role of major institutions in contributing to and perpetuating sexual violence
Examine how writing can be used to support survivors of violence and transform a rape culture
Evaluate strategies for preventing sexual violence and transforming a rape culture in the context of interlocking oppressions
